name: Hulesk

anatomy.part: tail tip, the thin far end of the eel's body on the left
mid-back, on the top edge at the thickest part of the body, where the hook line leaves the belly below it
neck, on the top edge where the body rises and the head bends down and to the right
upper jaw tip, the upper point of the torn mouth at the right
lower jaw tip, the lower point of the torn mouth, hanging below and left of the upper jaw
the hook bead on the trailing line at the end of the hanging line
the barb of the hook at the end of the trailing line

myth: Kael the Netter casts off the Lamp Road for fallen stars, as he always has, and as always he came up with nothing but salt. Then one summer his net came up heavy and torn. In the knot of it was an eel as long as a boat, with a mouth like a net that somebody had chewed. Her name is Hulesk. She swallows hooks and lines whole, and the boats came home with nothing but frayed rope and cursing. Orrun, beneath both seas, laughed until the water rolled. Aun said, let her hang in Vel where the boats can see her, so they will know what they are feeding. So Hulesk hangs there with her tail at Sóvar and her jaws open, and the hooks are still in her belly, down at Kárel where the line runs out. Mend your nets by her light, my grandmother says. And never trust a mouth that smiles.
verse:
Torn net in the dark
the eel ate the hook and line
mend by her cold light
